lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is the San Miguel County BOCC meeting on August 5th, where commissioners will hold public hearings on three Land Use Code amendments — including changes to who qualifies as a 'Qualified Owner,' a wildfire-area code update, and a continued hearing on nonconforming lots. Those are the kinds of decisions that quietly reshape what gets built and where in this county for years to come. The TMVOA board also meets July 31st to vote on officer elections and proposed changes to its fiscal policies, and Ouray County's Planning Commission is holding a virtual work session the same day as the BOCC to dig into possible rewrites of their Land Use Code definitions.

notable.stake: Three public hearings on Land Use Code changes affecting ownership rules, wildfire areas, and nonconforming lots.
